pointers.sentence: The innermost layer of the chain is not a middleware but a method of the handler (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

`BaseHandler.resolve_request` picks a resolver, asks it to match the request's `path_info`, which is the path without the script prefix, and stores the answer, a `ResolverMatch`, on the request as `HttpRequest.resolver_match`; it unpacks into the view and its positional and keyword arguments (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.resolve_request`) ([Resolving a path](../urls/resolving.md#a-resolvermatch-attribute-by-attribute)).
When nothing matches, the resolver raises `Resolver404`, a subclass of `Http404` (`django/urls/exceptions.py:Resolver404`).

If one returns a response, the loop stops and the view is not called; the response goes on through the rest of this method as if the view had returned it (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

A middleware's `process_request` runs before the handler has resolved the URL, and is not told which view the request is for; `process_view` runs after, just before the view is called, and is handed the view itself (`docs/ref/request-response.txt`, `docs/topics/http/middleware.txt`).

A middleware's `process_request` runs before the handler has resolved the URL, and is not told which view the request is for; `process_view` runs after, just before the view is called, and is handed the view itself (`docs/ref/request-response.txt`, `docs/topics/http/middleware.txt`).

`CsrfViewMiddleware` does its checking here for that reason: whether a view is exempt is an attribute of the view ([The CSRF check: `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`](../security/csrf-check.md)) (`django/middleware/csrf.py:CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`).

Before the call, `BaseHandler.make_view_atomic` wraps the view in `django.db.transaction.atomic` for each database whose settings have `"ATOMIC_REQUESTS"` true, unless the view was marked to be left out for it, as [Transactions: autocommit, `atomic` and savepoints](../connections/atomic.md#atomic_requests-and-non_atomic_requests) shows; an async view it refuses with `RuntimeError` instead of wrapping it (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.make_view_atomic`).

The transaction is around the view and nothing else: the middleware run outside it, and so does the rendering of a template response, later in this method (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

An `Exception` it raises is offered to the `process_exception` hooks, innermost first, by `BaseHandler.process_exception_by_middleware`, until one answers: its response replaces the view's; if none answers, the exception is raised again and leaves the centre for the wrapper around it ([How an exception becomes a response](exceptions.md)) (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.process_exception_by_middleware`).
Each raises a `ValueError` whose message names the view (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.check_response`) ([What the handler asks of a view](../views/callable.md#what-a-view-may-return)).

`check_response` stands after the `try` that surrounds the view, not inside it, so its `ValueError` is never offered to the `process_exception` hooks: it leaves the centre at once, and the wrapper around the centre sends `got_request_exception` and ordinarily makes a 500 (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

An exception raised while rendering is offered to the `process_exception` hooks too: `render` is called inside a `try` of its own, a response from one of them is returned as it is, and if none answers the exception is raised again out of the centre (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).
The documentation asks a hook to return a response with a `render` method (`docs/topics/http/middleware.txt`), but nothing checks: `render` is called on any response the last hook returned.
